items.prompt: What is the Sun?

options.text: a planet
options.why: The Sun is not a planet. Earth is a planet.

options.text: a moon
options.why: A moon orbits a planet. The Sun does not.

options.text: a star
a cloud of fire around Earth
options.why: The Sun is a star, far away from Earth.

hints: The Sun makes its own light and heat.
At night we can see others like it, far away.
They twinkle in the night sky.
items.explanation: The Sun is a star. It is the closest star to Earth, which is why it looks so big and bright.

items.prompt: What causes day and night?

options.text: The Sun moves around the Earth every day.
options.why: It looks like the Sun moves, but really the Earth spins.

options.text: The Moon blocks the Sun at night.
options.why: The Moon does not cause night.

options.text: Clouds cover the Sun at night.
options.why: Clouds come and go. They do not cause night.

options.text: The Earth spins on its axis.

hints: The Sun stays still compared to the Earth.
The Earth is turning all the time.
Is your side of the Earth facing the Sun or away from it?
items.explanation: The Earth spins on its axis. The side facing the Sun has day, and the side facing away has night.

items.prompt: How many days does the Earth take to travel once round the Sun in a normal year?
hints: This is the length of a normal year.
A leap year has one more day.
It is a little more than 360.
items.explanation: The Earth takes about 365 days to go once round the Sun. That is one year.

items.prompt: Match each movement to the time it takes.
pairs: the Moon orbits the Earth once
the Earth orbits the Sun once
hints: The shortest movement gives us one day.
A year is the longest.
The Moon's orbit takes about a month.
items.explanation: The Earth spins once in about 24 hours. The Moon orbits the Earth in about 4 weeks, and the Earth orbits the Sun in about 365 days.

items.prompt: Why does the Sun seem to move across the sky during the day?

options.text: The Earth is spinning.
The Sun orbits the Earth every day.
options.why: The Earth orbits the Sun, and that takes a whole year.

options.text: The wind blows it along.
options.why: Wind cannot move the Sun.

options.text: The Moon pulls it.
options.why: The Moon does not move the Sun.

hints: Think about sitting on a spinning playground ride.
The things around you seem to move past.
Which is really moving: you or them?
items.explanation: The Earth spins, carrying us with it. This makes the Sun seem to rise, cross the sky and set.

items.prompt: When it is 6 a.m. in Jakarta, it is 8 a.m. in Jayapura in Papua. Why does the Sun rise earlier in Papua?

options.text: Papua is closer to the Sun.
options.why: Papua and Jakarta are almost the same distance from the Sun.

options.text: Papua is further east, and the Earth spins from west to east.
The Sun moves faster over Papua.
options.why: The Sun does not move across the Earth. The Earth spins.

options.text: Clocks in Papua are set wrong.
options.why: The clocks are set on purpose, to match the Sun.

hints: The Sun rises in the east.
Find Papua and Jakarta on a map of Indonesia.
Which one turns to face the Sun first?
items.explanation: The Earth spins from west to east, so places further east turn to face the Sun first. Papua is far east of Jakarta, so its morning comes earlier.

items.prompt: The Moon shines brightly at night. Where does its light come from?

options.text: It makes its own light.
options.why: The Moon is not a light source.

options.text: It reflects light from cities on Earth.
options.why: City lights are far too weak to light up the Moon.

options.text: It reflects light from the Sun.
It is on fire.
options.why: The Moon is cold rock. It is not burning.

hints: The Moon is not a light source.
Something else lights it up.
What lights up the daytime sky?
items.explanation: The Moon does not make its own light. It reflects light from the Sun.

items.prompt: Sort these. Is each one a star, a planet or a moon?
hints: A star makes its own light.
Planets orbit the Sun.
A moon orbits a planet.
items.explanation: The Sun is a star. Earth, Mars, Jupiter and Venus are planets that orbit the Sun, and our Moon orbits the Earth.

items.prompt: When it is daytime in Indonesia, it is night-time in Brazil. Why?

options.text: The Sun switches off over Brazil.
options.why: The Sun shines all the time.

options.text: Brazil is in the Moon's shadow.
options.why: The Moon's shadow does not cause night.

options.text: Brazil is further from the Sun.
options.why: Distance from the Sun is not what makes night.

options.text: Indonesia faces the Sun while Brazil faces away.

hints: Brazil is on the other side of the Earth.
Only half of the Earth faces the Sun at a time.
Which side has day?
items.explanation: Brazil is on the opposite side of the Earth from Indonesia. When Indonesia faces the Sun, Brazil faces away and has night.

items.prompt: Put these in order of size, smallest first.
hints: The Moon orbits the Earth.
The Sun is a star.
Stars are enormous.
items.explanation: The Moon is smaller than the Earth, and the Sun is far bigger than both. More than a million Earths could fit inside the Sun.

items.prompt: Why does the Moon seem to change shape during a month?

options.text: We see different amounts of its sunlit half as it orbits the Earth.
The Earth's shadow covers part of it.
options.why: This is a common mistake. The Earth's shadow only falls on the Moon during an eclipse.

options.text: Clouds cover part of it.
options.why: The shapes change even on clear nights.

options.text: The Moon grows and shrinks.
options.why: The Moon is always the same size.

hints: The Sun always lights half of the Moon.
The Moon moves around the Earth.
From Earth, how much of the lit half can we see?
items.explanation: Half of the Moon is always lit by the Sun. As the Moon orbits the Earth, we see different amounts of the lit half, so its shape seems to change.

items.prompt: Draw the Sun and the Earth. Shade the half of the Earth that has night.

criteria.label: Draws the Sun to one side of the Earth
Shades the half of the Earth facing away from the Sun

hints: Draw the Sun on one side of the page.
The side of the Earth facing the Sun is lit.
items.explanation: The half of the Earth facing the Sun has day. The half facing away is in darkness, so it has night.

items.prompt: The Earth spins on its ___ once every 24 hours.
hints: It is an imaginary line.
It goes through the North and South Poles.
Think of a spinning top.
items.explanation: The Earth spins around an imaginary line called its axis. One spin takes about 24 hours.

items.prompt: Label the diagram of the Solar System.

figure.alt: A yellow Sun in the middle. A small blue Earth sits on an oval path around the Sun on the right. The oval path goes all the way round the Sun.

hints: Tap a label, then tap its number.
The Sun is at the centre.
The oval path is where a planet travels.
items.explanation: The Sun is at the centre. The Earth travels round the Sun along its orbit.

items.prompt: The Sun lights the Earth from the left. Tap the side of the Earth that has night.

figure.alt: The Sun is on the left with rays pointing at the Earth. The left half of the Earth is bright. The right half of the Earth is dark.

hints: The Sun lights only one half of the Earth.
Night is on the side facing away from the Sun.
Look at which half is dark.
items.explanation: The side facing away from the Sun is dark, so it has night.

items.prompt: Dewi marks the shadow of a stick three times in the day. Tap the picture with the shadow made at midday.

figure.alt: Three sticks with shadows. In A the Sun is low on the left and the shadow is long, pointing right. In B the Sun is high and the shadow is very short. In C the Sun is low on the right and the shadow is long, pointing left.

hints: The Sun is highest at midday.
A higher Sun makes a shorter shadow.
Find the shortest shadow.
items.explanation: At midday the Sun is highest in the sky, so the shadow is shortest. This is picture B.

items.prompt: A stick casts a shadow that is measured through the day. The pattern is balanced around midday. Complete the table.
head: Time
Shadow length (cm)
hints: Compare 10 a.m. with 12 noon.
The same time before and after midday gives the same height of Sun.
2 p.m. is 2 hours after midday, like 10 a.m. is 2 hours before.
items.explanation: The Sun has the same height 2 hours before and 2 hours after midday. So 2 p.m. matches 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. matches 8 a.m.

items.prompt: The Sun seems to rise in the east. Which way does the Earth spin to make this happen?

options.text: From east to west
options.why: That would make the Sun rise in the west.

options.text: From west to east
From north to south
options.why: The Earth does not spin in that way.

options.text: It does not spin at all
options.why: The Earth spins once every day.

hints: The Sun is not moving round the Earth.
Imagine standing on the spinning Earth.
You are carried towards the Sun in the east.
items.explanation: The Earth spins from west to east. Places turn towards the Sun in the east, so the Sun seems to rise there.

items.prompt: Putri sees the Moon in the blue sky in the afternoon. Why can we sometimes see the Moon by day?

options.text: The Moon makes its own light.
options.why: The Moon only reflects sunlight.

options.text: The Moon sometimes comes out of the Sun.
options.why: The Moon does not come from the Sun.

options.text: The Moon is above the horizon and lit by the Sun.
The Sun is switched off for a while.
options.why: The Sun is always shining.

hints: Where does moonlight come from?
The Sun lights the Moon all the time.
The Moon can be in the daytime sky too.
items.explanation: The Moon is lit by the Sun. At some times of the month it is in the sky during the day, so we can see it.

items.prompt: Put these Moon shapes in order as the Moon grows from new to full.
hints: The lit part grows bigger.
Start with the Moon you cannot see.
End with a full circle.
items.explanation: The lit part we see grows each night: new, crescent, half, then full.

items.prompt: The Moon goes round the Earth once in about 28 days. How many times does it go round in 84 days?
hints: Think of sharing days into groups of 28.
Divide 84 by 28.
28 + 28 + 28 is how many?
items.explanation: 84 days make 3 groups of 28 days. So the Moon goes round the Earth 3 times.

items.prompt: The Earth goes round the Sun once in 365 days. How many days is that for 3 times round?
hints: That is the same as 3 years.
Multiply 365 by 3.
items.explanation: 3 × 365 = 1095, so it takes 1095 days.

items.prompt: Match each space object to its description.
pairs: a star that gives us light and heat
hints: Stars make their own light.
Planets go round the Sun.
The Moon is Earth’s companion.
items.explanation: The Sun is a star. Earth and Jupiter are planets. The Moon orbits the Earth.

items.prompt: Which objects make their own light and which only reflect it?
hints: Stars are like our Sun.
Planets and moons do not make light.
A reflected light can be seen at night too.
items.explanation: Stars make their own light. The Moon and planets are seen only because they reflect light from the Sun.

items.prompt: The Earth travels round the ___ once every year. The ___ travels round the Earth.
hints: The centre of our Solar System is a star.
A natural satellite orbits a planet.
One year is one orbit.
items.explanation: The Earth orbits the Sun in one year. The Moon orbits the Earth.

items.prompt: Leo says night happens because the Earth moves away from the Sun, then back for daytime. Which fact shows he is wrong?

options.text: At the same moment it is day in one country and night in another.
The Moon is bright at night.
options.why: This does not tell us about the Earth’s distance.

options.text: The Sun is a star.
options.why: This does not explain day and night.

options.text: The Earth has an atmosphere.
options.why: This does not explain day and night.

hints: Think about two countries at the same moment.
If the whole Earth moved away, would some places still have day?
Compare Indonesia and Brazil.
items.explanation: If night were caused by distance, the whole Earth would have night at once. In fact one half is lit while the other half is dark, as the Earth spins.

items.prompt: When it is 9 a.m. in Jakarta, Makassar is one hour ahead and Jayapura is two hours ahead. Complete the table. Write times like 9:00 a.m.
head: City
Clock time
hints: Places in the east see the Sun first.
Add one hour for Makassar.
Add two hours for Jayapura.
items.explanation: Makassar is 1 hour ahead, so it is 10:00 a.m. Jayapura is 2 hours ahead, so it is 11:00 a.m.

items.prompt: Rina uses a torch as the Sun and a ball as the Earth. How can she show one whole day and night?

options.text: Move the torch round the ball once
options.why: The Sun stays still while the Earth turns.

options.text: Spin the ball once round its own axis
Move the ball far away and back
options.why: Distance does not cause day and night.

options.text: Cover the torch with her hand
options.why: The Sun does not turn off.

hints: A day and night are caused by the Earth spinning.
The torch stays still.
The ball turns once on its own.
items.explanation: A day and night cycle takes one full spin of the Earth. So Rina spins the ball once while the torch stays still.

items.prompt: Sunlight comes from the left. Tap the half of the Moon that is lit.

figure.alt: The Sun is on the left with rays pointing at a large grey Moon. The left half of the Moon is bright and the right half is in shadow.

hints: The lit half faces the Sun.
The Sun is on the left side.
Look for the bright part.
items.explanation: The half of the Moon facing the Sun is lit. The other half is in shadow because the Moon makes no light of its own.

items.prompt: Which statement about the Moon is correct?

options.text: The Moon makes its own light.
options.why: The Moon only reflects light from the Sun.

options.text: The Moon is a star.
options.why: The Moon is a natural satellite, not a star.

options.text: The Moon orbits the Earth.
The Moon is bigger than the Earth.
options.why: The Moon is smaller than the Earth.

hints: Think about what a moon does.
Compare sizes.
The Moon goes round something.
items.explanation: The Moon orbits the Earth. It is smaller than the Earth and shines only by reflecting sunlight.

items.prompt: True or false: The Earth spins once on its axis every 24 hours.

options.text: True
False

hints: How long is a day?
Which side faces the Sun?
One spin is one day.
items.explanation: The spin makes day and night, because the side facing the Sun has day.

items.prompt: True or false: The Sun moves around the Earth each day.

options.text: True
False

hints: What really spins?
It looks like the Sun moves.
The Earth spins.
items.explanation: The Earth turns, which makes the Sun seem to move across the sky. The Sun seems to rise and set because of the Earth's spin.

items.prompt: True or false: The Moon takes about one month to orbit the Earth.

options.text: True
False

hints: How long is a month?
Is it one day or one month?
About a month.
items.explanation: The Moon goes around the Earth in about 27 to 29 days.

items.prompt: True or false: The Moon makes its own light.

options.text: True
False

hints: What lights the Moon?
Is it a star?
It reflects sunlight.
items.explanation: The Moon only reflects light from the Sun.
